methodology: A fresh, adversarial re-read of the full production diff (git diff 8c53115 41ab563 -- lib/) against the mission's Section 28 checklist, performed as a separate pass from the implementation work itself - inspecting the actual diffs and tests, not self-certifying the design documents already written.

checklist.riotSpecificStringsOrBehavior: NONE FOUND. Grepped the full lib/ diff for Riot/Coinbase/Final Maturity Date/Collateral Documents/Security Confirmation/Day Count Fraction - all 4 matches are inside comments explaining root-cause provenance (citing docs/post-3f2-generalization-architecture-decision.json), never in string literals, conditionals, or branch logic.
checklist.benchmarkSpecificConditionals: NONE FOUND. No `if (packageKey === ...)`, no company/document-ID string comparisons tied to a specific package anywhere in the diff.
checklist.packageNameOrSectionNumberBranching: NONE FOUND. relationship-resolution.ts's regex changes (AGREEMENT_REF_RE determiner set, SUPERSEDING_QUALIFIER_RE) are generic English/legal-drafting patterns with no embedded section numbers, party names, or dates - confirmed generalizing correctly on a wholly synthetic 3-document chain (Zenith Robotics/Meridian Capital) using different terminology, dates, and amounts than Riot's real documents.
checklist.hiddenLegalTermDictionaries: NONE FOUND. completeness-check.ts's QUOTED_TERM_BEFORE_MEANS_RE is a single syntactic regex (quoted phrase + means/shall mean) with zero enumerated terms. No lookup table, no covenant-concept list, anywhere in the diff.
checklist.firstItemCardinalityCollapse: NONE FOUND. Confirmed by direct code reading that definitions[]/rules[] were already unbounded arrays before this remediation (no change needed to fix a cardinality defect); Unit A's fix is purely additive (prompt instruction + completeness detector). Verified via the 20-test suite's multi-sibling-definition assertions (A1/A2/A3/A4).
checklist.deterministicCodeInventingSemantics: NONE FOUND. checkDefinitionCompleteness only ever reports presence/absence of a citation pattern - it never manufactures a definition's content, calculationExpression, or IR. computeOperativeDocument only ever reports graph structure (which document, if any, is the un-superseded end) - it never infers what a document's operative content is.
checklist.unsafeDefinitionCompletenessAssumptions: NONE FOUND. The check requires POSITIVE citation evidence to fire (never fires on zero detections); verified via A5 (complex definition doesn't false-positive) and 5 additional adversarial hardening tests (nested quotes, 'shall mean', multi-sentence bodies, case/whitespace variance, legitimately-zero-detection sections).
checklist.weakenedVerifierThresholds: NONE - lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-verification/verify.ts is NOT in the changed-files list at all (confirmed via git diff --stat). The verifier's own 143-test suite passes unchanged, confirming independence was never touched.
checklist.recitalReferenceFalsePositives: NONE FOUND - checked via B9 (PKG-01 regression: an unrelated cross-default recital mention stays excluded from AMENDS resolution) and confirmed via the real Riot replay (see 08b-riot-package-graph-replay.json) that the broadened regex correctly fires ONLY on genuine agreement self-references, not incidental cross-references.
checklist.fuzzyRestatementGuessing: NONE FOUND. The chronological-predecessor fallback only engages behind an explicit textual qualifier (SUPERSEDING_QUALIFIER_RE) and only resolves when EXACTLY ONE same-type candidate exists before the source's own date - ties (B7/B8) and zero-candidate cases correctly stay UNRESOLVED/null, never a guess. Independently reproduced on the real Riot documents.
checklist.statusOverclaiming: NONE FOUND. computeOperativeDocument requires a non-null target for every relevant restatement effect to even attempt resolution, and additionally requires the resulting graph to have exactly one un-superseded terminal node (no forks, no cycles) before returning RESOLVED. The real Riot replay independently demonstrates this: a genuine data-quality defect elsewhere in the pipeline (document-classifier.ts misclassifying doc-a) produces a cyclic graph, and the code correctly reports REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than confidently asserting either document as operative.
checklist.staleDocumentLeakage: NONE FOUND. B14/B15 (synthetic) and the real Riot replay (08b) both confirm predecessor documents are never asserted operative, and the pre-existing node-supersession mechanism (buildNodeSupersessionIndex/getNodeSupersessionStatus) is untouched and still called identically by the same production code path.
checklist.unwiredProductionPaths: CLOSED (this remediation's own purpose for Unit B3): orchestrator.ts's analyzeInstrument now computes unresolvedTargetEffectsForThisInstrument and passes it into computeOperativeContractState - verified present in the actual diff (git diff shows the exact new lines in orchestrator.ts), not merely described in a design doc.
checklist.testsExercisingOnlyHelperFunctionsNotRea: PARTIALLY MITIGATED, DISCLOSED: B11's own test comment explicitly states it mirrors orchestrator.ts's exact line rather than driving the full Postgres-backed runContractAnalysis end-to-end, because operativeState/operativeDocument are not currently exposed on RunContractAnalysisResult's return shape - a pre-existing gap unrelated to Unit A/B. This is an honest, disclosed limitation of the test's reach, not a false claim of full end-to-end coverage; the REAL Riot regression replay (08b) independently exercises buildPackageGraph/runAmendmentPipeline/computeOperativeDocument together on real production data, which is a stronger integration signal than any unit test alone.

additionalObservationsBeyondChecklist: The real Riot replay surfaced a genuine, PRE-EXISTING, OUT-OF-SCOPE defect in document-classifier.ts (doc-a misclassified as COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE due to an Exhibit E 'Form of Compliance Certificate' table-of-contents mention). This is disclosed in 08b-riot-package-graph-replay.json and NOT fixed here, per the mission's explicit scope boundaries - flagging it for a future, separately-scoped architecture decision is the correct action, not silently patching it inside this remediation.
verdict: NO BLOCKER FOUND. All Section 28 checklist items pass; the one partial-coverage item (B11's non-full-Postgres-path caveat) is honestly disclosed by the test itself and independently offset by the real-Riot-data replay evidence.
